steps.name: Sample structure QC
caveats: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.
Do not scale, transform, or normalize the counts before the model; downstream normalization happens through DESeq2 size factors (median of ratios).
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-with-deconvolution-mouse-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 mouse gene symbols x 12 samples, gene-level counts from Salmon; the provenance does not state whether length correction occurred) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-deconvolution-mouse-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows, condition column: anti-PD-1 vs isotype control). Mus musculus (taxon 10090), subcutaneous tumors. This step runs before any model; counts are used as-is, with no pre-normalization.
steps.question: Do the 12 sample columns of counts.csv (12,000 mouse genes) match the 12 rows of metadata.csv one-to-one (6 anti-PD-1 vs 6 isotype control, unpaired, single batch), and how do the samples cluster by condition — specifically where does sample_01 sit, whose library size is ~4x below the median?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf.

constraints: Run the variance-stabilizing transformation blind to the design (transform = vst_blind), PCA on the 500 highest-variance genes (n_top_genes = 500), and a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap, all colored by condition.
low_depth_policy = keep_inspect_report: keep sample_01 through QC and report it; do not remove it for depth alone.

Before normalizing, inspect whether the count matrix is integer or fractional and state the inferred Salmon import state (integer -> summed gene-level counts; fractional -> length-corrected), and report per-sample library sizes, detected-gene counts, and DESeq2 size factors.
Verify the row names parse as mouse (MGI) gene symbols and report the fraction that do not.
steps.description: Verifies the 12-sample 6-vs-6 design against the 12,000-gene count matrix, produces blind-vst PCA and a distance heatmap colored by condition, and inspects sample_01 (low depth) without dropping it.
acceptance_criteria: All 12 metadata rows join 1:1 to the 12 sample columns, 6 anti-PD-1 and 6 isotype control.
PCA and distance heatmap colored by condition are produced and saved, with sample_01 visible on both.
Per-sample QC table (library size, detected genes, size factor) saved; sample_01 reported with an explicit keep/drop decision (drop only for a stated reason other than depth).
The inferred Salmon import state (integer vs fractional counts) is stated in the QC output.

steps.name: Low count filter + size-factor normalization
caveats: Do not pre-scale the counts; DESeq2 applies the size factors inside the model.
steps.context: Apply the pre-filter to the 12,000 x 12 count matrix from T1S1's input. Smallest group holds 6 samples (anti-PD-1 and isotype control, n=6 each). The filtered gene set and the size factors feed T1S3 (report); the scoring step T3S2 is wired to T1S1's unfiltered matrix per the procedure and recomputes its own size factors on it.
steps.question: How many of the 12,000 mouse genes keep at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size), and what are the median-of-ratios size factors for the 12 samples?

grounding.reason: Low count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples per R-0002@087b; normalization inside the model via median-of-ratios size factors per R-0026@9ab1.

constraints: normalize: size_factors = median of ratios (DESeq2 estimateSizeFactors) on the filtered matrix; depth_policy = size_factors_account_for_depth (a depth difference alone is not a reason to drop a sample).
steps.description: Pre-filters genes (>=10 counts in >=6 samples) and computes median-of-ratios size factors for the 12 samples; feeds the report and establishes the normalization basis.
acceptance_criteria: Number of genes before/after filtering reported; filtered matrix saved.
Size-factor table for all 12 samples, with sample_01's size factor reported beside the others.

steps.name: Descriptive immune + stromal cell-type scores per sample (mouse marker sets)
caveats: Do not run a human deconvolution method on mouse data. The marker sets and the reference profiles of MCP-counter, xCell, EPIC, and quanTIseq come from human samples, and a mouse symbol that maps to a human marker does not carry the same specificity in mouse tissue. The mouse tool of record is mMCP-counter, the mouse version of MCP-counter with markers from mouse data, and it is absent from this pool. Stop the deconvolution and ask for mMCP-counter or for a mouse reference, or give a descriptive signature score from mouse marker sets with the caution that it is not a deconvolution.
sample_01's library size is ~4x below the median: its marker scores carry more noise; keep it in the table and mark it, do not exclude it.
PanglaoDB covers human and mouse in one table: filter strictly to species 'Mm' rows before scoring; mixing in human markers is an R-0136 violation.
A score can rise from increased cell abundance OR from increased activation state of a resident population; do not interpret it as a pure fraction.
steps.context: The knowledge service flagged this step (rule R-0136@b81f): no mouse deconvolution reference is available in this environment — mMCP-counter is absent and the reference store holds no mouse reference profile (verified: the cell-typing references staged here are human-only, except the PanglaoDB marker table, which carries curated mouse ('Mm') markers) — and human deconvolution methods (MCP-counter, xCell, EPIC, quanTIseq) are forbidden on mouse data. Per the flag outcome (mouse_reference_required_or_descriptive_markers), this step implements the descriptive branch: a per-cell-type, per-sample marker score, not a deconvolution. Reference data needed: a curated mouse cell-type marker gene panel — resolve against the provisioned PanglaoDB marker table (release 2020.03.27, gzipped TSV with a species column), filtering strictly to species 'Mm'; symbols are MGI and should match the Salmon mouse gene symbols in counts.csv. Stromal types (fibroblast, endothelial, epithelial/tumor) may have sparse mouse coverage — report per-cell-type marker coverage and mark any cell type with fewer than 3 matched markers as unassessable rather than scoring it zero. DESeq2 is imported only to recompute median-of-ratios size factors on the unfiltered matrix (the procedure wires this step to T1S1, not T1S2).
steps.question: For each of the 12 samples (including sample_01), what are the immune and stromal cell-type scores from mouse marker sets, and how many markers of each cell type are present in the 12,000-gene matrix?

grounding.reason: flagged by R-0136@b81f: no mouse deconvolution reference is present in this environment and human deconvolution methods are forbidden on mouse data; the step implements the flag's outcome branch — descriptive signature scores from mouse marker sets (PanglaoDB 'Mm'), not a deconvolution.

constraints: Do not run MCP-counter, xCell, EPIC, or quanTIseq (human methods; forbidden on mouse data by R-0136).

deconvolution_input = linear_tpm_or_cpm: compute per-sample size factors (median of ratios, DESeq2) on the unfiltered 12,000 x 12 matrix from T1S1 and score on linear-scale CPM; do not feed a log-transformed matrix to any score.

composition_role = outcome_or_covariate_stated: state in the output that the cell-type scores play the role of the OUTCOME in this analysis (the research question is the composition itself); there is no differential-expression design in this plan.
report_composition_beside_de = true: report the composition table (there is no DE table in this plan, so the composition table stands alone).

Score definition: per cell type and sample, the median of linear-scale CPM over the cell type's matched markers; report the number of matched markers per cell type; state the transform beside every result.
Include all 12 samples; do not drop sample_01 (flag it as low-depth in the table).
steps.description: FLAGGED central step: per-sample immune and stromal cell-type scores from the provisioned mouse marker panel (PanglaoDB, species 'Mm', MGI symbols) on linear-scale CPM. Explicitly a descriptive marker score, not a deconvolution, because no mouse deconvolution reference exists in this environment (rule R-0136).
acceptance_criteria: Per-cell-type x per-sample (12) score table for every immune and stromal cell type with >= 3 matched mouse markers, plus a coverage table (matched marker counts per cell type).
A heatmap of the scores colored by condition (anti-PD-1 vs isotype control).
The output explicitly states that these are descriptive marker scores, not deconvoluted cell proportions, and names the reason (R-0136: no mouse deconvolution reference in this environment).

steps.name: Group comparison of cell-type scores: anti-PD-1 vs isotype control
caveats: With n=6 per group, only large and consistent shifts are detectable; do not over-read individual p-values — report the BH q.
A cell-type score difference conflates abundance and activation; frame the result accordingly.
steps.context: Input: the T3S2 per-cell-type x per-sample score table plus the condition column of metadata.csv (anti-PD-1 vs isotype control, unpaired, n=6 per group, single batch). Cell types marked unassessable in T3S2 (< 3 matched markers) are reported as 'not assessable' rather than tested.
steps.question: For each immune and stromal cell type assessed in T3S2, do the per-sample scores differ between the 6 anti-PD-1 and the 6 isotype-control tumors?

grounding.reason: no rule covers a two-group comparison of per-sample marker scores; Wilcoxon rank-sum with BH correction and a seeded permutation sensitivity analysis chosen from standard practice

constraints: Per cell type: two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test on the 12 scores (unpaired); report the median score per group, the median difference (anti-PD-1 minus isotype control), the rank-biserial correlation as effect size, the p-value, and the BH-adjusted q across cell types.
Sensitivity: permutation test (10,000 label permutations, fixed seed) on the same table; record the seed in the output.
State the limited power (n=6 per group) in the output.
steps.description: Per-cell-type two-group comparison of the T3S2 scores between 6 anti-PD-1 and 6 isotype-control tumors: Wilcoxon rank-sum, median difference, rank-biserial effect size, BH-FDR, and a seeded permutation sensitivity analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Per-cell-type results table: n per group, median per group, median difference, Wilcoxon p, BH q, rank-biserial correlation, permutation p.
The output states that the comparison is on descriptive marker scores, not on deconvoluted proportions.

steps.name: Report
caveats: Do not claim a mechanism of anti-PD-1 response beyond the composition differences observed; the scores are association evidence only.
steps.context: Aggregate T1S1 (QC summary, design verification, sample_01 decision, inferred Salmon import state), T1S2 (genes kept, size factors), T3S2 (score + coverage tables, flagged limitation), and T3S3 (group comparison).
steps.question: What should the final report state about the immune and stromal composition of the 12 mouse tumor samples and the anti-PD-1 vs isotype-control difference?

grounding.reason: no rule covers this step; the reproducibility-record setting follows R-0086@becf as returned by the service

constraints: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version, annotation_release (PanglaoDB 2020.03.27 release; DESeq2 1.52.0; seed of the T3S3 permutation sensitivity analysis).

The report must state: (1) the cell-type values are descriptive marker scores, not proportions, per R-0136 (no mouse deconvolution reference in this environment); (2) provisioning mMCP-counter or a mouse reference profile would enable a true proportion-based deconvolution of the same samples; (3) the scoring-input transform (linear-scale CPM via median-of-ratios size factors); (4) the keep decision and QC metrics for sample_01.
steps.description: Final report: QC summary (incl. sample_01), filter/size-factor results, per-sample immune/stromal score table, group-comparison table, coverage table, and the reproducibility record — with the flagged limitation stated prominently.
acceptance_criteria: A single report with the QC summary, the score table (all 12 samples), the group-comparison table, the coverage table, and the reproducibility record.
No table or figure labels the scores as fractions/proportions.

plan.title: Mouse tumor immune/stromal composition, anti-PD-1 vs isotype
plan.analytical_narrative: Twelve mouse subcutaneous tumor bulk RNA-seq samples (6 anti-PD-1 vs 6 isotype control, unpaired, single batch) with a 12,000-gene Salmon count matrix (length correction unverified) and one low-depth sample (sample_01, ~4x below median library size). Flow: (1) T1S1 QC the sample structure with blind DESeq2 vst, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap colored by condition — verifies the 6-vs-6 design, the mouse symbol space, and the inferred Salmon import state; sample_01 is kept because the question asks for every sample's composition and removal would require a stated reason beyond depth. (2) T1S2 pre-filters genes (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size) and computes median-of-ratios size factors — size-factor CPM is the normalization basis because Salmon's length correction is unverified. (3) T3S2 is the central step and it is FLAGGED: knowledge rule R-0136 forbids human deconvolution methods (MCP-counter, xCell, EPIC, quanTIseq) on mouse data and records that no mouse deconvolution reference is present in this environment (verified against the reference store: human-only cell-typing references plus the mouse PanglaoDB marker panel). Per the flag outcome, T3S2 computes descriptive immune and stromal cell-type scores per sample from the mouse marker set (PanglaoDB, species 'Mm', MGI symbols) on linear-scale CPM — explicitly reported as marker activity, not cell fractions. (4) T3S3 tests, per cell type, whether the scores differ between anti-PD-1 and isotype control (Wilcoxon rank-sum, BH-FDR, seeded permutation sensitivity). (5) T1S3 aggregates everything with a reproducibility record and states the limitation: provisioning mMCP-counter or a mouse reference profile would convert the scores into a true proportion-based deconvolution.

Low count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples
descriptive marker-based cell-type scoring from mouse marker sets (PanglaoDB species Mm) on linear-scale CPM; flagged substitute, no human deconvolution method

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

Do not run a human deconvolution method on mouse data. The marker sets and the reference profiles of MCP-counter, xCell, EPIC, and quanTIseq come from human samples, and a mouse symbol that maps to a human marker does not carry the same specificity in mouse tissue. The mouse tool of record is mMCP-counter, the mouse version of MCP-counter with markers from mouse data, and it is absent from this pool. Stop the deconvolution and ask for mMCP-counter or for a mouse reference, or give a descriptive signature score from mouse marker sets with the caution that it is not a deconvolution.
